title: Ordinary tensor comparison for completed constant modules
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative ring and d a ProEtaleAdicCoefficientDatum on A. Let O be adicDatumRing X d, G be completedKoszulConstant X d, and c:O to G(A) be completedKoszulOne X d, characterized by the section 1 tensor 1 [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. With the existing sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there is an isomorphism of curried bifunctors tau:G(M tensor N) to G(M) tensor G(N). Its regular-module component satisfies c followed by G of the inverse right unitor of A and tau(A,A) equals the inverse left unitor of O followed by c tensor c. This statement concerns ordinary modules only and includes no complexes or change of site.

proof.text: Form the actual constant presheaf functor P used by adicLisseConstantModules: constant modules on the one-object category followed by pullback to the pro-etale site. The sectionwise identity gives a natural isomorphism tensor followed by P to P times P followed by tensor. Whisker this isomorphism with module sheafification and compose with the inverse of the pro-etale sheafification tensor comparison. This gives an uncurried natural tensor isomorphism for F=adicLisseConstantModules.

For E=completedConstantExtension, use the object and map equalities of derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients to transport each tensorIso from scalarExtension_constraint_coherence to E. Naturality follows by substitution of the map equality, cancellation of equality transports, the naturality field of the scalar-extension data and functoriality of tensor. Whisker the comparison of F with E and the comparison of E with F times F, and compose to obtain e:tensor followed by G isomorphic to G times G followed by tensor.

Prove that the prescribed map c=completedKoszulOne is invertible. The ordinary scalar-extension/restriction adjunction, module sheafification Hom equivalence and regular-module/sections equivalence give a natural bijection Hom(G(A),N) to sections(N). The specified section formulas for the ordinary adjunction unit and c show that this bijection is precomposition with c followed by the unit-module/sections bijection: evaluate both at 1 on each site object. Precomposition with c is therefore bijective for every N, so the coyoneda criterion gives IsIso c.

Normalize the comparison using only monoidal coherence. For an automorphism a of the tensor unit I, the maps sigma_Y=lambda_Y inverse followed by a tensor identity_Y followed by lambda_Y form a natural automorphism of the identity functor. Whisker exchange and unitor naturality prove naturality. At I, equality of the left and right unitors and right-unitor naturality give sigma_I=a. Let z be c followed by G(rho_A inverse) followed by e_(A,A), and let w be lambda_I inverse followed by c tensor c; both are isomorphisms I to G(A) tensor G(A). Choose a=w followed by z inverse. Postcompose every component of e by sigma at its target. Naturality on z gives z followed by sigma_target=sigma_I followed by z=w. Curry this natural isomorphism, obtaining the asserted tau and exactly the required regular-module equation. All constructions use isomorphisms and universal properties and include the zero ring and empty site.

theorem completedConstantModuleTensor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A]
    (d : ProEtaleAdicCoefficientDatum A) :
    let O := adicDatumRing X d
    let G := completedKoszulConstant X d
    let c := completedKoszulOne X d
    letI := SheafOfModules.isMonoidal_W_independentCoefficients O
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory O
    ∃ τ : (Functor.postcompose₂.obj G).obj (curriedTensor _) ≅
        (((Functor.whiskeringLeft₂ _).obj G).obj G).obj (curriedTensor _),
      c ≫ G.map (ρ_ (ModuleCat.of A A)).inv ≫
        (τ.hom.app (ModuleCat.of A A)).app (ModuleCat.of A A) =
          (λ_ (𝟙_ (adicDatumModules X d))).inv ≫ (c ⊗ₘ c)
